chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:
Surely Allah, Blessed and Exalted, disciplined His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله). Then when He brought him to what He intended, He said to him:
Indeed, you are surely upon a magnificent character.
So He entrusted to him His religion, and He said:
Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.

And surely Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ordained the obligatory shares and did not assign anything to the grandfather, while the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) allotted to him one-sixth. So Allah, Majestic is His remembrance, approved that for him; and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without account.

key_terms.أَدَّبَ: disciplined and refined through divine تربیة
key_terms.الْجَدِّ: the grandfather in the context of inheritance
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضَ: the obligatory apportioned shares, here in inheritance law
key_terms.دِينَهُ: His religion, meaning the divinely ordained religious order
key_terms.نَبِيَّهُ: His Prophet, Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was divinely authorized in matters of religion and legal judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, perfected the discipline and character of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and then entrusted to him authority in the religion. It presents the Prophet’s legislative and directive authority as divinely sanctioned, and illustrates this through the ruling concerning the grandfather’s inheritance share. The cited Quranic passages are used to show both the Prophet’s عظیم character and Allah’s authorization of his binding guidance.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Educated His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So when He<sup>azwj</sup> Ended up with him<sup>saww</sup> to what He<sup>azwj</sup> Wanted, Said to him<sup>saww</sup>
[68:4] And you are upon magnificent morals.
So He<sup>azwj</sup> Authorised to him<sup>saww</sup> His<sup>azwj</sup> Religion, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Said
[59:7] and whatever the Rasool gives you, accept it, and from whatever he forbids you, keep back.

And that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Necessitated the necessities (of the inheritances) and did not apportion anything for the grandfather, and that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> fed (apportioned to) him, the sixth. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention, Allowed that for him<sup>saww</sup>, and these are the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[38:39] This is Our Gift, therefore give out freely or withhold, without accountability’.
en.sarwar: 6.Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “
Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, disciplined and educated His Prophet to the level that He wanted and said, “
“O Muhammad, you certainly possess a great degree of moral discipline and education. [64:4].
The He made him the in charge of His religion and said, “
. .what the Messenger (of Allah) you, you must take (obey) and what he prohibits you, you must desist from. .” [59:7]

Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, declared the laws of inheritance and did not assign any part for the grandfather. The Messenger of Allah assigned one sixth for him. Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, granted permission in the matter in His words as follows. “
This is our gift to you, you may grant it others or keep it without being held responsible [38:39]”
